items.why: The report says both bands "soften monotonically with power" and that "Both bands also broaden." It adds that "The Si line is fixed within 0.05 cm-1" and puts the shifts down to "laser heating, not ... a change in the sample's strain or doping."
It gives "dT = 1.81/0.016 = 113 K from G and 5.11/0.034 = 150 K from 2D" for 5 mW against 0.5 mW, which is close to the rubric's ~125 K, but it never gives the ~50 K rise at 2 mW.

It reports the "Slope d(2D)/d(G) = 5.11/1.81 = 2.8 ± 0.2" against a "Strain line slope 2.2 ± 0.2" (Lee 2012) and "0.034/0.016 = 2.1" expected for heating. It then warns that the 5 mW spectrum "would be misread as roughly 0.08 % tensile strain" and calls this "the trap."

It says to "Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for strain and doping" and extrapolates linearly to zero power. It also states that heating and strain are degenerate in the G-2D plane, so spectra at different powers cannot be compared directly.

It recommends to "repeat it at lower power" and notes that "0.5 mW is itself probably heated slightly, by tens of K." It also asks for "spot size and objective NA ... to quote power density (not power)."

It takes the 0.5 mW spectrum (G 1581.3, 2D 2669.5 cm-1) as the reference and says it is "close to neutral and unstrained." It corrects the 2D origin to 532 nm by dispersion ("about 2669 cm-1, which matches") and flags that estimate as uncertain.

wrong_claims.why: The report says the shifts come from "laser heating, not from a change in the sample's strain or doping." It mentions annealing or photo-doping only as caveats that were not tested.
It recommends the lowest-power (0.5 mW) spectrum even though it notes that spectrum has the "lowest SNR."
